openwashdata is an active global community that applies the FAIR principles to data from the water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) sector, and teaches the skills to do it.

::: {.owd-actions} [Explore the data](pages/gallery/data/index.qmd){.btn .btn-primary} [Join the course](pages/academy/index.qmd){.btn .btn-outline} ::: ::: {#subscribe}

::: ::: ::: ::: ::: {.owd-section} ## Dataset of the month ::: {.owd-dotm} ::: {.owd-dotm-text} **solidwastekampala** holds the quantity and composition of domestic solid waste from 103 households in Kampala, Uganda, weighed over one week in three parishes of low, middle and high income by researchers at Makerere University. Waste per person rises with income, from 0.43 to 0.98 kg per day, and food makes up three quarters of the mass. [Open solidwastekampala](https://openwashdata.github.io/solidwastekampala){.owd-more} ::: ::: {.owd-dotm-chart} ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](index_files/figure-html/dataset-of-the-month-1.png){fig-alt='Stacked bar chart of the share of household waste mass by category for the low, middle and high income parishes in Kampala. Food makes up 75 to 82 percent in each parish. Garden and wood, plastics and polythene, other waste, paper and textiles, and glass and metals share the rest.' width=672} ::: ::: ::: ::: ::: ::: {.owd-tint} ::: {.owd-section} ## Learn

ds4owd, our free online course, teaches WASH professionals data science in R. Two cohorts have graduated so far.

We are currently preparing the sign-up forms for the third iteration, which starts around September 2027. In the meantime, you can browse the course website of the second cohort from 2025.

[Course website of the 2025 cohort](https://ds4owd-002.github.io/website/){.owd-more} [About the course](pages/academy/index.qmd){.owd-more} ::: ::: ::: {.owd-section} ## Read
